_comment: Per-provider tool-name rewrite rules + idiom translation notes applied to agent and command bodies at render time. Source bodies use Claude Code tool names (capitalized) and Claude idioms (e.g. 'Load skills/X/SKILL.md', 'spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/X.md'). The renderer uses tool_rewrites to describe the tool-name mapping, and idiom_notes to describe the brighter conventions for skill loading and subagent spawning.

claude._comment: Identity — source already uses Claude Code tool names and idioms.

opencode._comment: opencode exposes lowercase tool names; the `task` tool spawns subagents; `question` is the quiz tool. Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash stay lowercase. Skills are loaded via the `skill` tool named `SKILL.md` filename form (e.g. `skill({ name: 'reviewer-mindset' })`). Subagents are spawned via `task({ name: '<agent-name>' })` — no path arg, the name only.
idiom_notes: · **Skill loading.** When the body says `Load skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md`, invoke the opencode `skill` tool with the skill's folder name, e.g. `skill({ name: '<name>' })`. The skill body lives at `.opencode/skills/dev-team-agents/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md` and opencode resolves it by name.

· **Subagent spawn.** When the body says `spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/<X>.md`, treat it as `task({ name: '<X>' })` in opencode — subagents are registered as `.opencode/agents/<X>.md` and resolved by name only, no path.

· **Project context paths.** References like `docs/`, `.dev-team-agents/user-data/preferences.json`, `.dev-team-agents/scripts/...` are real paths materialized at install time; access them with the `read` tool the same way Claude would.

codex._comment: Codex surfaces differ between CLI, app, and evolving runtime builds. The renderer therefore maps Claude idioms to Codex concepts, not to a brittle single tool roster. AskUserQuestion maps to request_user_input in Plan mode, but the rendered fallback depends on the command metadata: operational commands must continue in normal conversation when the chooser is unavailable; only plan-first commands keep the /plan retry requirement. Skills are read as files at .dev-team-agents/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md.
idiom_notes: · **Codex-native equivalents.** Use the file, shell/search, subagent, plan/todo, and web tools available in the current Codex surface. Tool names can differ between CLI, app, and newer runtime builds; prefer the current-session equivalent over the literal Claude name in the source body. When the source body calls for a structured user-choice step, use `request_user_input` in Plan mode.

· **Structured-choice fallback is command-specific.** If `request_user_input` is unavailable, follow the rendered command's own policy: operational commands ask the same question directly in conversation, preserving the same options and recommended path; plan-first commands keep the `/plan` retry requirement.
· **Skill loading.** When the body says `Load skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, open and read `.dev-team-agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` or the matching category path with the current file-read tool.

· **Subagent spawn.** When the body directs you to spawn an agent, use the current Codex subagent mechanism to invoke the agent defined at `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`. Resolve agents by name, not by a Claude path.

· **Project context paths.** References like `docs/some-file.md`, `.dev-team-agents/user-data/preferences.json`, and `.dev-team-agents/scripts/...` are real files. Read them with the current file-read tool.

· **Plan gate.** For complex or architectural tasks, use Codex's plan mode or the current-session planning mechanism. Only commands whose rendered policy marks structured choices as required should force the task back to `/plan`.
· **Task arguments.** `$ARGUMENTS` in this prompt = the user's free-form input after the slash command. Use it as the task description.
